Ailment

/AYL-ment/ — rhymes with nail sent · noun

Hear It

What It Means

An ailment is a minor illness or health problem that someone suffers from, often one that lingers without a clear cause.

Grandpa blames every ailment, from sore knees to hiccups, on the weather.

Worked Example

Mrs. Chen has suffered from a persistent knee stiffness for three months, but doctors can't identify any specific disease; it simply won't go away.

Ailment perfectly captures this situation — a minor, lingering health problem without a clear diagnosis. A more formal word like 'disease' wouldn't fit because there's no identified condition; 'problem' is too vague.

How Ailment Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

illness

illness: a general state of being sick

disease

disease: a serious, defined medical disorder

condition

condition: an ongoing health problem or state

Antonyms

health

health: sound, disease-free condition of the body

vigor

vigor: strong, active physical health and energy

How Strong Is It? — discomfort → ailment → illness → disease

discomfort vs. ailment

discomfort vs. ailment: Discomfort is weaker than an ailment; discomfort is mere unease, while an ailment is an actual minor illness someone suffers from.

illness vs. ailment

illness vs. ailment: Illness is stronger than an ailment; an ailment is a small, often lingering health problem, while an illness is a more serious sickness.

disease vs. ailment

disease vs. ailment: Disease is far stronger than an ailment; a disease is a serious, defined medical condition, while an ailment is only a minor complaint.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — ail

Root — ail: to trouble, afflict, make sick (Old English)

Suffix — -ment

Suffix — -ment: state or condition (noun-forming) (Latin/French)

Put it together

Put it together: Ail means 'to trouble or afflict' and -ment marks a state or condition, so an ailment is the condition of being troubled by a (usually minor) illness.

Use the root in a new word: ailing

Use the root in a new word: ailing: A person who is ailing suffers from some ailment; both are built on the old verb 'ail,' meaning to trouble or afflict.

Word Building

Word Choice

neutral

Ailment is the go-to word for minor, nagging health problems — especially ones without a clear diagnosis. It's conversational and kind, avoiding the weight of 'disease' while being more specific than the generic 'illness.'
